title: Runtime fidelity experiment recipes and execution patterns
author: Priya Raman
content:
Summary
-------
This page collects reproducible experiment 'recipes' and execution patterns for evaluating runtime fidelity (model output quality vs cost/latency) and how those choices interact with kernel scheduling, profiling instrumentation, and our benchmarking suite. The intent is to provide a small set of repeatable, reviewable experiments teams can run before changing default fidelity or scheduling policies in production.

Scope and goals
----------------
- Audience: runtime engineers, performance SREs, model-onboarding owners, and product owners evaluating tradeoffs.
- Goals:
  - Provide reproducible experiment steps that exercise fidelity tiers (high/medium/low) against representative workloads.
  - Capture instrumentation and profiling guidance so results are comparable across teams.
  - Describe the interaction surface between scheduling hints and fidelity fallbacks.
  - Include a triage checklist and runbook for common regression signals.

Owners and contacts
-------------------
- Page owner: Priya Raman (runtime-performance)
- Primary reviewers: Ethan Morales (serving-runtime), Lina Chen (profiling), Marco Alvarez (benchmarks)
- Slack channel: #runtime-fidelity

Experiment recipes (overview)
----------------------------
Each recipe below follows the same pattern: objective, prerequisites, configuration (as we-run YAML snippet), step-by-step procedure, metrics to capture, pass/fail criteria, and common failure modes.

1) Fidelity smoke: small-batch quality vs latency sweep
   Objective: Measure token-level latency and sample quality variation between fidelity tiers for a fixed prompt set.

   Prereqs:
   - model variant family loaded (e.g., redwood-open-8b, redwood-v2-7b-quant)
   - bench client >= 1.4.0 on bastion
   - golden prompt set s3://redwood-experiments/fidelity/golden-100.txt

   Config (example runtime route override, minimal YAML):
   ---
   route: fidelity-smoke-test
   model_variant: redwood-open-8b
   fidelity_profiles:
     high: {quantize: false, kv_cache: write-through, decode_samples: 1}
     medium: {quantize: int8, kv_cache: writeback, decode_samples: 1}
     low: {quantize: int4, kv_cache: disabled, decode_samples: 1}
   concurrency: 16
   sequence_p95_limit: 256
   ---

   Steps:
   1. Deploy route override using `rctl apply -f fidelity-smoke.yml --env=staging`.
   2. Warmup: run `bench client warmup --route fidelity-smoke-test --duration 3m`
   3. Run sweep: for each fidelity profile run `bench run --route fidelity-smoke-test --prompts golden-100.txt --concurrency 16 --duration 10m --trace`
   4. Collect outputs to s3: `bench collect --dest s3://redwood-results/fidelity/smoke/$profile/`

   Metrics to capture:
   - per-request p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side and client-side)
   - tokens-per-second and GPU utilization (nvidia-smi per-host + runtime kernel counters)
   - sample-level quality: BLEU/ROUGE and task-specific scorer (or human eval sample set)
   - trace IDs for any requests > p99 latency

   Pass criteria:
   - High->medium quality delta < 4% by primary scorer while medium latency reduction >= 20% and cost-per-token improves >= 18%

2) Kernel hint A/B: preemption vs cooperative windowing
   Objective: Evaluate effect of scheduler hinting (preemptive-priority vs cooperative-window) on tail latency under mixed short/long workloads.

   Prereqs: scheduler feature flag `hint:kernel_priority_v2` enabled on test fleet pool.

   Config (policy snippet):
   ---
   scheduler_policy: |
     priorities:
       - name: interactive
         credit: 100
         preemptive: true
         window_ms: 20
       - name: batch
         credit: 10
         preemptive: false
         window_ms: 200
   ---

   Steps:
   1. Create two test pools with identical hardware; enable policy A (preemptive for interactive) in pool-1 and policy B (cooperative windowing) in pool-2.
   2. Use `rbench mixed-shape --short 50% --short-rt 10-50ms --long 50% --long-rt 400-800ms --duration 30m --trace` to reproduce mixed traffic.
   3. Compare p95/p99 tail and kernel queue length metrics from runtime kernel telemetry.

   Expected observations:
   - Preemptive policy typically lowers p95 for short requests but may increase kernel churn (kernel-switch counts rise by 15–40%).
   - Cooperative windowing reduces overall context-switch churn at the expense of longer p99 for short requests under high long-request load.

   Triage tip: If kernel-switch counts increase dramatically (>100% baseline) and GPU occupancy drops, enable `kernel_backpressure_sampling` and collect detailed traces as described in the Profiling section.

3) KV-cache warmstart experiment
   Objective: Quantify warmup period and hit-rate dynamics for KV cache strategies across fidelity profiles.

   Steps:
   1. Start with empty pool; route requests that mimic conversational traffic (session affinity on).
   2. Run for 90 minutes and record per-session hit-rate, mean latency, and memory pressure stats.

   Metrics to capture: hit-rate over time (per-session and aggregate), byte-eviction rates, model-serving p50/p95 over warmup window.

Instrumentation and profiling guidance
------------------------------------
- Baseline profiling flags (recommended): `--telemetry=full --kernel-sampler=1/100 --trace-mode=shadow`
- Flamegraph capture: run `rt-prof --trace-id $TRACE --output flame-$TRACE.svg`. Use the sampled user+kernel timeline to identify kernel scheduling hot spots.
- When collecting traces for regression triage include the following: runtime logs (json), kernel telemetry export (prometheus snapshot), GPU metrics (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv), and bench client logs.

Sample CLI snippet (end-to-end):
```
rctl apply -f fidelity-smoke.yml --env=staging
bench client warmup --route fidelity-smoke-test --duration 3m
rbench mixed-shape --route fidelity-smoke-test --concurrency 16 --duration 10m --trace > mixed.out
rt-prof collect --trace-file mixed.out --out /tmp/rtprof
rt-prof flame /tmp/rtprof -o /tmp/flame.svg
```

Benchmarking suite integration
------------------------------
- Use the canonical harness `rbench` and the workload signatures in s3://redwood-bench/signatures. When adding new signatures:
  1. Include a short, medium, and long sequence template.
  2. Provide an expected token distribution and a golden scorer if applicable.
  3. Register the signature in the benchmark catalog with owner and date.

- Example benchmark config table (plain CSV view):
  name,concurrency,duration,seq_p95_limit,workload_signature,owner
  fidelity-smoke,16,10m,256,golden-100.txt,priya
  mixed-longshort,64,30m,512,mixed-shape-v2,marco

Runtime config requirements (table)
--------------------------------
- Minimum: 8 vCPU job agent, 64GB host RAM, 32GB GPU ram (A100-40G recommended)
- Kernel telemetry: telemetry-v2 enabled (retain 72h)
- Profiles: capture at least 1/100 sampled traces for production parity

Regression triage runbook (short)
--------------------------------
1. Observe signal: elevated p95/p99, increased error-rate, or quality regression.
2. Check deployment diff: recent route overrides, scheduler policy changes, model-variant swaps.
3. Run `bench replay --trace-ids <p99-trace-ids> --baseline <prev-run>` to reproduce in a shadow pool.
4. Collect artifacts: trace + runtime logs + kernel telemetry + GPU metrics.
5. Run `rt-diff` to get per-span latency deltas and `kvcache-hitrate-report` for cache regressions.
6. If kernel scheduling is implicated: escalate to kernel-scheduling owners (label: kernel-scheduling) with artifacts and short summary (include p95 delta and kernel-switch counts).

Common failure modes and mitigations
-----------------------------------
- Short-run sampling bias: If sequence lengths < 16 tokens, sampler under-represents hot paths. Mitigation: increase `--kernel-sampler` to 1/10 for short-run experiments.
- Small-batch oscillation under swap pressure: small batches cause frequent kvcache eviction thrashing on memory-constrained hosts. Mitigation: pin session affinity to fewer hosts and increase `kvcache.reserve_mb` by 30%.
- Kernel-hint bitmask misapplication: observed where a plugin sets a priority bit but forgets to clear on error leading to permanent elevated priority. Mitigation: add guard in FFI shim to reset hint on error path (PR template included below).

Quick PR template for kernel-hint guard
---------------------------------------
- Title: kernel: guard-clear-hint-on-error (short description)
- Description: ensure scheduler hint bitmask is cleared on all error return paths for FFI calls to kernel_hint_set.
- Test plan: unit tests for error path, integration smoke with `rbench mixed-shape` to ensure no increased priority leak.

Release note snippet (if experimental becomes default)
----------------------------------------------------
- Added fidelity experiment recipes and scheduler interaction guidance. Teams should run the fidelity smoke before flipping `default_fidelity=medium` to avoid unexpected quality regressions.

Appendix: example JSON result artifact layout
--------------------------------------------
- results.json (metadata + aggregated numbers)
- traces/ (directory of trace JSONs)
- flamegraphs/ (SVGs)
- bench-raw/ (raw bench client stdout)

Notes and references
--------------------
- See also: execution-contracts-and-stable-fallbacks-2026 (runtime execution guarantees)
- Profiling playbook: telemetry-feedback-kernel-autotune-playbook-2026 for autotune loop guidance

If you use these recipes please add a short note under this page (EDIT history) with your experiment id and a 2–3 line outcome.
